the bicategory of graphs, and the bicategory of graph spans, are a natural setting for a study of reachability, and minimization and realization of processes, with functorial aspects, and with applications to concurrency and model-checking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an abstract theory for the minimization and minimal realizability in spans of graphs.

the span ( graph ) model of processes can be used as a model of computation, with the reachability relation as a semantics, and with the minimization and minimal realizations as the computational primitives.

the bicategory of graph spans has a natural notion of minimality for morphisms, and that the minimal morphisms are precisely the ones which are minimal with respect to a notion of reachability, in the sense that the span is a minimal representation for its source object.
The main takeaway from our work is that
minimization is functorial, but minimal realization is only functorial up to isomorphism.
